persona: Simulated beginner: casual video creator new to music production, aiming for a 30-second ambient soundtrack.
outcome: Saved DUSK.rill and received successful UI confirmations for DUSK.wav and DUSK.mid. Arranged startup audio with manually drawn MIDI chords assigned to Rill Lab Sine VST3. Final displayed arrangement duration is 30.134 seconds. Earlier playback reported 3119 plug-in/render failures, so audible VST success remains unverified.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: The empty-area hint, pencil, duplicate, time ruler, and named exports supported task completion in roughly eight minutes. Editing notes required discovering a right-click action, and precise trim endpoints took several attempts.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: Consistent dark interface, restrained colors, clear waveform and MIDI previews, and large readable controls felt polished.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Most mouse edits responded promptly and the sketch was quick to build. Preparing audio and a roughly real-time WAV export added waiting; playback failed with a large error count.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Note editing was not opened by my initial double-click, edge drags did not land exactly where expected, and the render error did not identify the failing instrument or explain the cause.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: The core requested audio, MIDI, VST assignment, save, WAV export, and MIDI export controls were present. Playback reliability was unresolved and the observed WAV dialog offered no visible format selector beyond effect tails.

findings.observation: Double-clicking the blank-area MIDI hint opened the device library; Assign instrument created the MIDI track and pattern, with Rill Lab Sine visibly identified as VST3.
findings.recommendation: Keep the explicit empty-area hint and clear Assign instrument action.

findings.observation: Double-clicking the pattern body appeared to leave the arranger unchanged. Right-click > Edit notes opened the piano roll.
findings.recommendation: Make note editing discoverable directly on the pattern, with a visible edit affordance or clear double-click behavior.

findings.observation: Dragging three note ends toward the same screen position left different note lengths. Arranger trimming first produced 30.402 seconds, and changing to 1 bar snap reduced the displayed length to 30.134 seconds rather than an exact 30.000.
findings.recommendation: Show a precise destination/time tooltip during resize and make snap behavior easier to predict for video-duration edits.

findings.observation: Both pattern and project rename flows offered an on-screen Keyboard. It allowed DUSK naming without physical typing. Save and export dialogs then suggested matching filenames.
findings.recommendation: Preserve these mouse-accessible naming controls and consistent filename defaults.

findings.observation: First playback stopped with Plug-in/render error, 3119 failures. Details repeated the error and listed platform/audio settings but did not identify a cause. I stopped, dismissed, and retried; I stopped the retry shortly afterward without establishing sustained playback success.
findings.recommendation: Identify the failing processing component and offer a targeted recovery action with an explanation a beginner can use.

findings.observation: File menu exposed WAV and MIDI exports. WAV showed duration, 48 kHz stereo 32-bit float, and effect tails; I disabled tails. Both exports later showed explicit success banners.
findings.recommendation: Keep explicit export confirmation; offer visible audio format choices for common video-editor delivery needs.

positives: The timeline shows bars and elapsed seconds together, making a video-length target easier to locate.
Pencil note drawing, clip duplication, Fit, and Previous/Next clip navigation were discoverable.
Mouse-only project naming and matching save/export filenames worked.
The final arrangement and both export confirmations were easy to see.
limitations: This is one independent agent simulation, not human usability research.
All app interaction used only the supplied mouse driver; no keyboard events, project injection, source inspection, or direct composition edits.
Only the supplied stock audio and Rill Lab Sine VST3 were exercised; no claims about other plug-ins.
No audio capture was auditioned. Musical quality and audible VST output were not assessed.
The lab uses software graphics and a timer-paced virtual audio sink with documented 60 ms buffering and a 1024-frame request at 48 kHz; no hardware latency conclusion is supported.
Project, WAV, and MIDI contents were not inspected. Artifact validity and rendered content require independent coordinator verification.
Final duration is approximately 30 seconds, not precisely 30.000 seconds.
